## Fresh product truth

Fresh GitHub Releases inspection found four releases newer than the starting website snapshot:

- `v1.0.18` at `f0ffd56cc7fa70a1de5fc7b814c87521a811cf4f`: agent usage and session analysis;
- `v1.0.19` at `1885b064c5a1133a7d7b4ad5e97e3cd134bfa2d4`: multi-machine organization overview and browser regression coverage;
- `v1.0.20` at `f7d961f86d57073013a58a8f72ea0528e8e63c38`: release-workflow safety only;
- `v1.0.21` at `412ee6dbad967fa48a226a8052ee0c689e4bd1c6`: current release, including explicit Google/GitHub sign-in provider-status behavior and installation/startup documentation.

The drift was materially user-facing:

- the signed-in hosted app now lands on **All machines** and aggregates bounded reachable-Node overviews in browser memory through Direct or Relay;
- Controller supplies machine directory/access policy but does not persist the fetched Node snapshots or the browser-produced fleet aggregate;
- machine/organization views expose observed Tokens, source-reported subscription windows, Agent Plans, CPU/RSS, and session state;
- observed token use and provider-reported capacity remain separate signals;
- a selected session now has three views — Conversation, Process Tree & AI Prompts, and Analysis — because Analysis replaces the old separate Timeline and Detailed Events tabs while retaining event inspection inside the timeline;
- supported hosted sign-in choices stay visible, with unconfigured providers disabled and explained rather than silently hidden.

The existing `/product/` and `/architecture/` canonicals already owned these reader decisions. No thin version-specific page was created.
